description: Mynt's Solana vulnerability database: one entry per vulnerability class. Entries with gate 'block' refuse a program on mainnet when a deterministic detection finds them; 'flag' entries are leads the audit agent must confirm or dismiss. Every detection that Mynt runs itself (source_pattern, idl_shape, bytecode_program_ref, dependency_advisory) is tested against the entry's bad and good fixtures. The audit and red-team agents get the whole database as their checklist. Changes land only by a reviewed pull request; propose_vulnerability_rule stores proposals for that review.

entries.title: Value moved through the token programs
entries.description: The program holds or moves tokens: it uses the SPL Token, Token-2022 or Associated Token programs (token accounts, transfers, mints, burns, approvals). Mynt refuses value-moving programs on mainnet for now: a program that controls token accounts can drain them.

detection.message: uses $1: token accounts and token CPIs aren't allowed on mainnet yet
calls the token program's $1 (a CPI that moves or controls tokens)

detection.scenario: Move tokens out of a token account the program controls without its owner's signature.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: SOL moved by system-program transfers or assigns
entries.description: The program transfers SOL or reassigns accounts through the System Program, often signing with its own PDAs (invoke_signed / CpiContext::new_with_signer), so it can move lamports out of accounts it controls.

detection.message: $1: a system-program transfer or assign

detection.scenario: Drain SOL from a PDA the program signs for, or reassign an account's owner.

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them
Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Lamports moved by hand between accounts
entries.description: The program edits account lamports directly (sub_lamports, add_lamports, lamports.borrow_mut()): a hand-written close or drain that can empty accounts it owns.

detection.message: $1: moves lamports directly between accounts

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Hard-coded admin key
entries.description: An instruction authorizes against a key written into the program (pubkey!, Pubkey::from_str, a const, an address = constraint), or the IDL pins a signer to a fixed address: a hidden admin that can act on everyone's accounts. Allowed only for Mynt's own mainnet signer, which no program should need.

detection.scenario: Act on another user's state with the program's admin path.

references.title: rekt.news: Raydium (a compromised admin key drained pools)
Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Authority handed to an account that doesn't sign
entries.description: An instruction sets an authority, admin or owner field to an argument or to an account that doesn't sign the instruction: authority can be handed (or taken) without the new holder's consent. This is also a one-step authority transfer: the safe pattern is a pending authority that must sign an accept step.

detection.scenario: Take over a victim's state by setting its authority field.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

also_covers: access_control: one-step authority transfer (no accept step)

entries.title: Account close pays a non-signer
entries.description: An Anchor close = target sends the closed account's lamports to an account that doesn't sign the instruction (or to a fixed address).

entries.title: Retained mint or freeze authority
entries.description: The program creates or controls a mint whose mint or freeze authority it keeps (or an admin keeps): supply can be inflated or holders' accounts frozen.

detection.message: $1: keeps the power to mint or freeze

entries.title: Token-2022 permanent delegate or transfer hook
entries.description: The program sets up or relies on Token-2022's permanent delegate (which can move or burn anyone's tokens of the mint) or a transfer hook (arbitrary code on every transfer).

detection.message: $1: a Token-2022 extension that lets one party move others' tokens or run code on every transfer

entries.title: Authority account that isn't required to sign
entries.description: An accounts struct takes an authority, admin or owner as a plain AccountInfo or UncheckedAccount without a signer constraint: anyone can pass the real authority's address without its signature.

detection.scenario: Call an authority-gated instruction passing the victim's authority address without its signature.

entries.title: Account data read without an owner check
entries.description: The program deserializes an AccountInfo's data by hand without checking which program owns the account: an attacker passes an account they created with forged data.

detection.message: deserializes an account's data without checking its owner

detection.scenario: Pass an account with forged data, owned by another program.

references.title: Halborn: explained, the Crema Finance hack (July 2022)

entries.title: Stored authority not matched to the signer
entries.description: An instruction takes a signer and a mutable account whose data records an authority of the same name, but never checks they match (no has_one, constraint or comparison): any signer can act on anyone's account.

detection.scenario: Sign with your own key and pass the victim's account.

entries.title: remaining_accounts used without checks
entries.description: The program reads ctx.remaining_accounts, which Anchor never validates, without checking their owners or addresses.

detection.message: uses ctx.remaining_accounts with no owner or address check in the file

detection.scenario: Pass arbitrary accounts as remaining accounts.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Account type not checked (type cosplay)
entries.description: The program deserializes account data without checking its discriminator, so an account of one type can be passed as another.

detection.message: $1: deserializes without checking the account's type

detection.scenario: Pass an account of another type with the same layout.

entries.title: PDA without the canonical bump
entries.description: The program derives a PDA with create_program_address and a bump it doesn't derive itself, so several addresses (one per bump) pass for the same seeds.

detection.message: create_program_address: the bump isn't the canonical one from find_program_address

detection.scenario: Derive the PDA with a non-canonical bump and pass it.

entries.title: PDA seeds without a fixed prefix (seed collision, PDA sharing)
entries.description: A PDA's seeds are a single caller-chosen value with no fixed prefix, so PDAs of different kinds, or of different users, can collide or be shared.

detection.message: PDA seeds are one caller-chosen value with no fixed prefix

detection.scenario: Create a PDA of one kind whose address another instruction accepts as a different kind.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Duplicate mutable accounts
entries.description: An instruction takes two mutable accounts of the same type without requiring them to differ, so passing the same account twice can double-count or overwrite state.

detection.scenario: Pass the same account for both mutable slots.

entries.title: Sysvar account address not checked
entries.description: The program reads a sysvar from an account the caller passes (Clock::from_account_info and the like) without checking its address, so a fake sysvar can be supplied.

detection.message: reads a sysvar from a caller-supplied account without checking its address

detection.scenario: Pass a fake sysvar account.

entries.title: Re-initialization or front-run initialization (init_if_needed)
entries.description: init_if_needed lets an instruction run on an account that already exists, and an initialization anyone can call first lets an attacker set up the account (or a singleton config) before its owner does.

detection.message: init_if_needed: the instruction also runs on an existing account; check it can't be re-initialized or initialized by someone else first

detection.scenario: Initialize the victim's account (or the program's config) first, or re-initialize it.

entries.title: Closed account that can be revived
entries.description: An account is closed by zeroing its lamports by hand without clearing its data or marking it closed, so it can be refunded within the same transaction and used again.

detection.message: closes an account by hand without wiping it

detection.scenario: Close an account and refund it in the same transaction, then use it again.

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Arbitrary CPI: the called program isn't checked
entries.description: The program invokes a program passed in by the caller (an AccountInfo or UncheckedAccount named as a program) without checking its id, so an attacker substitutes their own program.

detection.scenario: Substitute your own program for the one the instruction calls.

entries.title: Signer privileges passed to an unchecked program
entries.description: The program signs a CPI with its PDAs (invoke_signed / new_with_signer) in a file whose instructions take the called program from the caller: the PDA's authority can be handed to an attacker's program.

detection.scenario: Make the program sign for its PDA in a call to your program.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Account data used after a CPI without reload
entries.description: After a CPI that can change an account, the instruction reads the account's deserialized fields without calling reload(), so it acts on stale data.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Instructions sysvar read without checking it (Wormhole)
entries.description: load_instruction_at reads instructions from whatever account is passed as the instructions sysvar; it is deprecated because it doesn't check the account. Wormhole lost $326M to a fake sysvar that 'proved' signatures were verified.

detection.message: load_instruction_at: reads the instructions sysvar without checking its address (use load_instruction_at_checked)

detection.scenario: Pass a fake instructions sysvar that claims a signature check happened.

entries.title: Instruction introspection that checks only the index
entries.description: The program inspects another instruction in the transaction (load_instruction_at_checked, get_instruction_relative) but never checks that instruction's program id, so any program's instruction at that index passes.

detection.message: introspects an instruction without checking its program id

detection.scenario: Put a look-alike instruction from your own program at the index the program inspects.

entries.title: Signed message without a nonce or expiry (signature replay)
entries.description: The program accepts an Ed25519 or secp256k1 signature checked through the instructions sysvar, but nothing in the file looks like a nonce, an expiry or a record of used signatures, so the same signed message can be replayed.

detection.message: $1: a signed message with no nonce, expiry or used-signature record in the file

detection.scenario: Submit the same signed message twice.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Signed message not bound to this program or cluster (cross-program / cross-cluster replay)
entries.description: The program verifies an off-chain signed message, but nothing in the file binds the message to this program's id or to a cluster, so a signature made for another program, or for devnet, can be replayed here.

detection.message: $1: a signed message with no program id or cluster in it

detection.scenario: Replay a signature made for another program or another cluster.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

also_covers: signatures: missing replay protection on off-chain signed messages

entries.title: Integer overflow or underflow
entries.description: Release builds wrap on overflow unless overflow-checks is on; wrapping_* / unchecked_* / overflowing_* arithmetic wraps silently either way.

detection.message: no Cargo.toml turns overflow-checks on for release builds
$1: arithmetic that wraps silently

detection.scenario: Drive a counter or balance past its bounds.

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Precision loss and rounding direction
entries.description: Floating point, or integer division before multiplication, loses precision; rounding in the user's favour can be repeated to drain value.

detection.message: $1: floating point or division before multiplication

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them
Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Division by a value that can be zero
entries.description: Integer division by a caller-influenced value panics when it is zero, failing the instruction (a denial of service where it matters).

detection.message: $1: division by a variable (checked_div makes the zero case explicit)

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Casting truncation
entries.description: An `as` cast to a narrower integer silently truncates (and to a signed type can flip sign).

detection.message: as $1: a cast that can truncate (use try_from)

references.title: Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Swap or trade without slippage bounds (front-running, sandwich)
entries.description: An instruction named like a swap, trade, buy or sell takes no minimum-out, maximum-in or slippage argument, so a front-runner can sandwich it.

detection.scenario: Sandwich the instruction: move the price before it and back after.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Oracle price used unchecked (stale, low confidence, manipulable)
entries.description: The program reads an oracle price without checking its age or confidence, or uses get_price_unchecked, so a stale or manipulated price drives its logic (Mango Markets lost $114M to price manipulation).

detection.message: $1: an oracle price with no staleness or confidence check in the file

detection.scenario: Move the oracle's price (or use a stale one) before the instruction runs.

references.title: Pyth: best practices for price feeds
CFTC: charges over the Mango Markets manipulation

entries.title: Timestamp or slot dependence
entries.description: Logic depends on Clock's unix_timestamp or slot, which validators can skew a little: fine for coarse deadlines, unsafe for fine-grained ordering or pricing.

detection.message: $1: depends on the cluster's clock

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Insecure randomness
entries.description: The program derives 'random' outcomes from the clock, the slot or recent blockhashes, which validators and callers can predict or influence.

detection.message: $1: randomness from on-chain values anyone can predict

detection.scenario: Predict the outcome and only send the transaction when it favours you.

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security
Neodyme: Solana smart contracts, common pitfalls and how to avoid them

entries.title: Unbounded vectors or loops
entries.description: Account state holds a Vec or String with no declared maximum, or the program loops over all remaining accounts without a bound: growth or input size can exhaust space or compute and lock the account.

detection.message: loops over every remaining account with no bound

references.title: Helius: a hitchhiker's guide to Solana program security

entries.title: Account growth or realloc abuse
entries.description: The program grows accounts (realloc) by caller-influenced amounts: rent can be pushed onto others or accounts grown past what the program can handle.

detection.message: $1: grows an account

entries.title: Compute exhaustion
entries.description: Open-ended loops (while, loop) can run past the compute budget for some inputs, failing the instruction for everyone who needs it.

detection.message: $1: an open-ended loop

entries.title: Account created without rent exemption
entries.description: The program creates accounts by hand with a lamport amount not taken from Rent, so they may not be rent-exempt and can be refused or purged.

detection.message: creates an account by hand with no Rent minimum in the file

entries.title: Dependency with a RustSec advisory
entries.description: A crate in the Cargo.lock the program was built with has a RustSec vulnerability advisory. Checked by cargo-audit in the gate's static analysis; the operator can accept an advisory that can't reach an on-chain program (PROGRAM_GATE_CARGO_AUDIT_IGNORE), shown in every report.
